newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Novolipetsk said planning share buyback.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Novolipetsk said planning share buyback.

text.p: A leading shareholder in Russia steelmaker Novolipetsk Metals Combine said the company is planning to buy back a 37.5 percent stake owned by a group of investors.

London-based Trans-World Group said Novolipetsky Metallurgichesky Kombinat (NLMK), which faces a court hearing over investor rights on Wednesday, was interested in purchasing the 37.5 percent held by a group of shareholders including Trans-World.

"There appears to be some interest from the plant to purchase our shares. The group is open to the proposition at an appropriate price," metal trading company Trans-World, a member of the shareholder group, said in a statement.
Senior managers at Novolipetsk were unavailable for comment on Tuesday.
The Trans-World statement said the 37.5 percent stake had been proxied to the factory, "because they are in the best position to know what's good for the plant".
Another group of investors has taken Novolipetsk to court because they say it has failed to observe their shareholders' rights, including the right to nominate members of the board of directors.
Sources familiar with the dispute questioned how Novolipetsk would now be able to fund the buyback.

Industry experts say Novolipetsk relies heavily on the London-based Trans-World, which sells it raw materials. Novolipetsk repays Trans-World with a finished product which is often sold at below market rates.

U.S. investment fund Cambridge Capital Management, the Sputnik fund, an investment arm of Renaissance Capital, and Bank MFK, associated with Uneximbank (Oneksimbank in Russian) are all involved in the cases against the plant.
The Federal Securities Commission is also investigating the company.
